items.followUp: A car travels at 12 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 0.5 m s⁻² for 20 s. Find the distance travelled and its final velocity.

rubric.why: Award for converting half a minute to 30 s and stating the distance equation.
rubric.description: Converts time and selects the equation for distance under uniform acceleration.
rubric.how: Check that the time is converted to seconds and the correct kinematics equation is written.
Award for the correct substitution/calculation and final distance, including the unit.

rubric.why: The final velocity is 16 m s⁻¹.
rubric.description: Uses the velocity equation and obtains the final velocity.
rubric.how: Check the equation, substitution using the given values, and final answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: u = 10 m s⁻¹, a = 0.2 m s⁻², t = half minute = 30 s.
Distance: s = ut + ½at².
Substitution: s = (10 m s⁻¹)(30 s) + ½(0.2 m s⁻²)(30 s)² = 300 m + 90 m.
Distance travelled: s = 390 m.
Final velocity: v = u + at = 10 m s⁻¹ + (0.2 m s⁻²)(30 s) = 16 m s⁻¹.

items.followUp: A force of 120 N acts on a 15 kg body initially at rest. Find the distance through which it acts to give the body a speed of 40 m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: Newton's second law gives an acceleration of 10 m s⁻².
rubric.description: Finds the acceleration from the applied force and mass.
rubric.how: Check that a = F/m is used with the given values.

rubric.why: This equation relates the initial velocity, final velocity, acceleration and distance.
rubric.description: Selects the appropriate equation of motion.
rubric.how: Award for writing the equation that can be used to find distance.

rubric.description: Substitutes the values correctly into the equation.
rubric.how: Check the initial velocity, final velocity and acceleration are substituted correctly.

rubric.why: Solving gives a distance of 125 m.
rubric.description: Calculates and states the distance through which the force acts.
rubric.how: Award for the correct distance with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 200 N, m = 20 kg, u = 0 m s⁻¹, v = 50 m s⁻¹.
Acceleration: a = F/m = (200 N)/(20 kg) = 10 m s⁻².
Equation: v² = u² + 2as.
Substitution: (50 m s⁻¹)² = (0 m s⁻¹)² + 2(10 m s⁻²)s.
Distance: s = 2500 m² s⁻² ÷ 20 m s⁻² = 125 m.

items.followUp: A force F makes an angle α with the horizontal x-axis. Write expressions for its horizontal and vertical components.

rubric.why: The horizontal component is adjacent to the angle θ, so it equals F cos θ.
rubric.how: Check that the component along the x-axis is expressed using cosine.

rubric.why: The vertical component is opposite to the angle θ, so it equals F sin θ.
rubric.how: Check that the component perpendicular to the x-axis is expressed using sine.

modelAnswer: Resolve F into perpendicular components along the x- and y-axes.
Horizontal component: Fₓ = F cos θ.
Vertical component: Fᵧ = F sin θ.

items.followUp: Define nuclear physics and atomic physics.

rubric.why: Atomic physics concerns atoms and their properties or structure.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the study of atoms, their structure or their properties.

rubric.why: Nuclear physics concerns the nucleus and nuclear phenomena.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the study of the nucleus, its properties or nuclear reactions.

modelAnswer: Atomic physics is the branch of physics that studies the structure and properties of atoms.
Nuclear physics is the branch of physics that studies the structure and properties of atomic nuclei and nuclear reactions.

rubric.why: Plasma is an ionized gas containing charged particles, including free electrons and positive ions.
rubric.description: Defines plasma as an ionized state of matter containing charged particles.
rubric.how: Award for identifying ionized gas or its free electrons and positive ions.

accept: p:application of physics to the earth
rubric.why: Geophysics applies physics to the study of the Earth.
rubric.how: Award for describing the use of physics to study the Earth.

modelAnswer: Plasma is an ionized gas consisting of free electrons and positive ions.
Geophysics is the branch of physics that applies the principles of physics to the study of the Earth.

items.followUp: Name two types of motion and give an example of each.

rubric.why: Any one valid type of motion earns this mark.
rubric.how: Accept any one of translatory, rotatory, vibratory or oscillatory motion.

rubric.why: A second valid type of motion earns this mark.
rubric.description: Names a second type of motion.
rubric.how: Accept a different type from the first mark: translatory, rotatory, vibratory or oscillatory motion.

modelAnswer: Two types of motion are translatory motion and rotatory motion.

items.followUp: Define momentum and write its mathematical relation.

rubric.why: Momentum is defined as the product of mass and velocity.
rubric.how: Award for stating that momentum depends on the product of mass and velocity.

rubric.why: The equation for momentum is p = mv.
rubric.how: Check that momentum is expressed as mass multiplied by velocity.

modelAnswer: Momentum is the product of the mass of a body and its velocity.
Its equation is p = mv.

items.followUp: State two situations in which friction is useful in everyday life.

rubric.why: Any one valid use of friction earns this mark.
rubric.description: States one advantage or useful effect of friction.
rubric.how: Accept examples such as walking without slipping, writing, gripping or holding objects, braking, or enabling vehicle movement.

rubric.why: A second valid use of friction earns this mark.
rubric.description: States a second advantage or useful effect of friction.
rubric.how: Accept a different valid example from the first mark.

modelAnswer: Friction between our feet and the ground enables us to walk without slipping.
Friction between the brakes and a vehicle's wheels helps the vehicle to stop.
